info.name: Sonatype Lifecycle Public REST Advanced Search Policy Violation Details API

params.name: p
params.description: Enter the policyIds to obtain the corresponding violation details

params.name: openTimeAfter
params.description: Enter the date (format YYYY-MM-DD) from which you want to retrieve the violation details

params.name: openTimeBefore
params.description: Enter the date (format YYYY-MM-DD) until which you want to retrieve the violation details

params.name: type
params.description: Set one or more policy violation type (active, legacy, waived) to include

items.docs:
Use this method to retrieve policy violation details for a policy/policies. You will need the policyId(s) to retrieve the policy violations details. policyId is available as the response field of the Policies REST API.

Permissions required: View IQ Elements

params.name: constituentId
params.description: Enter the violationId. Use the GET method described for the endpoint /api/v2/policyViolations to obtain the policy violationId.

items.docs:
A cross-stage policy violation represents an aggregate of all violations of a policy  occurring across multiple stages of an application. Cross-stage policy violations are helpful in performance analysis by determining the time taken to remediate a violation across all stages where it was detected.
Use this method to retrieve all cross-stage violations, irrespective of the time they were detected.

Permissions required: View IQ Elements

params.name: violationId
params.description: Enter the policy `violationId`. Use the GET method described for the endpoint /api/v2/policyViolations to obtain the policy violationId.

items.docs:
A cross-stage policy violation represents an aggregate of all violations of the same policy, occurring at multiple stages for an application. Cross-stage policy violations are helpful in performance analysis by determining the time taken to remediate a violation across all stages where it was detected.
Use this method to retrieve cross-stage policy violations.

Permissions required: View IQ Elements

params.name: ownerType
params.description: Possible values are 'application' or 'organization'

params.name: ownerId
params.description: Possible values are applicationId, organizationId

params.name: stageId
params.description: Possible values are 'develop', 'source', 'build', 'stage-release', 'release', and, 'operate'.

params.name: componentIdentifier
params.description: Enter the component identifier and the coordinates of the component for which you want to obtain the transitive violations. This is optional, not required if package URL or hash value is provided.

params.name: packageUrl
params.description: Enter the package URL of the component. This is optional, not required if component identifier or hash value is provided.

params.name: hash
params.description: Enter the hash value of the component. This is optional, not required if component identifier or package URL is provided.

items.docs:
Use this method to obtain all transitive policy violations for a given component in  a specific stage. Transitive policy violations are violations caused by transitive dependencies.

Permissions required: View IQ Elements

params.name: ownerType
params.description: Enter the scope for this violation. Possible values are 'application'

params.name: ownerId
params.description: Enter the identifier for the scope specified above. E.g. applicationId

params.name: scanId
params.description: Enter the scanId/reportId corresponding to the scan.

params.name: componentIdentifier
params.description: Enter the component identifier and the coordinates of the component for which you want to retrieve the transitive policy violations. This is optional, not required if package URL or hash value is provided.

params.name: packageUrl
params.description: Enter the package URL for the component for which you want to retrieve the transitive policy violations in the specific scan.

params.name: hash
params.description: Enter the hash value for the component for which you want to retrieve the transitive policy violations in the specific scan.

items.docs:
Use this method to retrieve transitive policy violations for a given component in a specific scan.

Permissions required: View IQ Elements

params.name: violationId
params.description: Enter the policy violationId for which you want to obtain the applicable auto policy waiver

items.docs:
Use this method to obtain the existing auto waiver applicable to a policy violationviolation.

Permissions required: View IQ Elements

params.name: violationId
params.description: Enter the policy violationId for which you want to obtain the applicable waiver requests.

items.docs:
Use this method to obtain all existing waiver requests that are applicable to a policy violation. A waiver request is considered as 'applicable' if it matches the following conditions:
  • The policyId for the policy violation matches the policyId associated with the waiver request
  • The violated policy conditions match the policy conditions of the waiver request/li>
  • The waiver request scope matches the violating component
Permissions required: View IQ Elements

params.name: violationId
params.description: Enter the policy violationId for which you want to obtain the applicable waivers.

items.docs:
Use this method to obtain all existing waivers that are applicable to a policy violation. A waiver is considered as 'applicable' if it matches the following conditions:
  • The policyId for the policy violation matches the policyId associated with the waiver
  • The violated policy conditions match the policy conditions of the waiver/li>
  • The waiver scope matches the violating component
Permissions required: View IQ Elements

params.name: violationId
params.description: Policy violation id to find similar waivers for.

items.docs:
Use this method to retrieve similar policy waivers for the given policy violation id.

Permissions required: View IQ Elements
